clue.text: We raised a bloom, a monster

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a bloom is a flower

explanation.surface: Gardeners boast of having grown a monstrous flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the flower upwards, as fits a down clue; the 'a' before 'monster' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolfman of folklore is a classic monster of horror stories.

clue.text: Community centre, by golly, oddly unattractive

indicators.note: the centre of the word community is its middle letter
oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of the word golly

explanation.surface: A community centre is declared, with an exclamation, to be strangely ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of the nine-letter 'Community' is U; 'oddly' takes GLY from 'golly'; 'by' just means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something unattractive is unsightly or plain to look at.

clue.text: Shakespearean king's daughter depicted by Stubbs

definitions.text: Shakespearean king's daughter depicted by Stubbs

parts.words: Shakespearean king's daughter depicted by Stubbs
parts.note: Cymbeline's daughter shares her name with the actress Stubbs, who portrays characters on stage, while the surface suggests George Stubbs the painter of horses

explanation.surface: A painting by George Stubbs shows a princess from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: Stubbs looks like the eighteenth-century painter, but the clue means the English actress of that surname, who 'depicts' roles by acting them.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Cymbeline, daughter of the king, bears this name, as does the actress Stubbs.

clue.text: Womble country

definitions.meaning: Great Uncle of that name is the eldest of the Wombles, furry creatures of a British children's TV series
a nation in south-eastern Europe on the Black Sea

explanation.definitionFit: Great Uncle of this name leads the Wombles, and it is also a Balkan nation with Sofia as capital.

clue.text: Successful prose pours out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer whose words flow freely is doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of PROSE and POURS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a successful person is thriving and well off.

clue.text: Intrude for an hour mid-morning

indicators.note: mid- attached to morning asks for the middle letters of that word

explanation.surface: Someone barges in for an hour in the middle of the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid' strips the first and last letters of MORNING, leaving ORNIN after H; 'for an' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to butt into something uninvited is to intrude on it.

clue.text: Oil producer making composer take a test

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer
the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles

explanation.surface: A composer sits an exam before he can make oil.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly vehicle safety test; 'making' and 'take' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: This citrus tree yields an aromatic oil used in perfume and Earl Grey tea.

clue.text: Old headmaster giving Orlando maths revision

indicators.note: revision means the letters are revised into a new order

explanation.surface: The setter revises maths with a headmaster of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' rearranges ORLANDO (the setter's own pseudonym) and MATHS into the twelve-letter name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian head of Rugby School was a famous reforming schoolmaster.

clue.text: Get out of bed for our pot shot?

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A gardener's pot breaks, so the plant must leave its bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get out of bed' suggests rising in the morning; here the bed is a flower bed. 'shot' rearranges OUR POT.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull a plant out of its bed by the roots is to dig it out entirely.

clue.text: Be very heartless in company

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letters of the word very

explanation.surface: Advice to be extremely cruel when among others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the central ER from VERY, leaving VY.
explanation.definitionFit: A group or gathering of people or birds can be called this word.

clue.text: Author having go as gender bender

indicators.note: a bender twists things, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer who chose to cross the gender line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bender' rearranges GO AS GENDER; fittingly, the French novelist wore men's clothes and took a man's pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin, nineteenth-century writer of Indiana.

clue.text: Monster with no drink to knock back?

indicators.note: knock back is read as turn backwards, reversing the whole phrase

parts.note: taken as written
grog is rum and water, a sailor's drink

explanation.surface: A dry party leaves a monster with nothing to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to knock back' looks like drinking, but it reverses NO GROG.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake-haired creature of Greek myth, such as Medusa, whose gaze turns people to stone.

clue.text: An officer is beginning to train one without special skills

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer
taken as written

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the opening letter of the word train

explanation.surface: An officer starts training a recruit who has no specialism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' gives T from 'train'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with broad knowledge rather than one specialism is the opposite of a specialist.

clue.text: In harmony with one in a new key

indicators.note: in places the letter for one inside another piece

parts.note: green means inexperienced or new
I is the Roman numeral one
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Being in tune with someone in an unfamiliar musical key.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside GREEN after A, then G ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: people in harmony are in accord or concurring.

clue.text: A painter is artificial, if not natural

indicators.note: artificial means made up, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A painter is said to be fake if he is not naturalistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artificial' rearranges the letters of IF NOT NATURAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri, a French painter of still lifes of flowers and group portraits, carried this double surname.

clue.text: Given a shiny loco without any rails

indicators.note: loco means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the word any is taken from the pool of letters

explanation.surface: A gleaming locomotive is delivered but has no track to run on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loco' looks like a train, but signals an anagram: GIVEN A SHINY, 'without' the letters of ANY, rearranges to the answer. 'rails' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail against something is to protest bitterly, a synonym for speaking out angrily.

clue.text: See 15
Making a noise? Jolly good!

definitions.meaning: an old British intensifier meaning very

explanation.definitionFit: The word means clattering noisily, and in dated British slang it means excellent or very.

clue.text: See 8
Burn more than a pirate

parts.note: to sear is to scorch or burn
over means more than, as in over a hundred

explanation.surface: A pirate captain burns more than his rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for a buccaneer who roams the ocean robbing ships.

clue.text: Shakespearean king's mother going up river or down under

indicators.note: in a down entry, the next piece goes underneath, so after
in a down clue, going up means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Nile is the African river
taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal mother travels up a river or off to Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' looks like Australia, but in a down entry it means the last piece sits below the reversed river; 'going up' reverses that river.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Eleanor of Aquitaine appears as King John's mother in Shakespeare's history play.

clue.text: Mock some travellers at Zeebrugge

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ridicule a few tourists arriving at a Belgian ferry port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock' is an adjective meaning imitation, not the verb to ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an imitation or substitute that is not the genuine article.

clue.text: Moving cautiously, say, to admit a transgression

indicators.note: to admit means to let something in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: EG, for example, is signalled by say
taken as written
a sin is a transgression

explanation.surface: Confessing a wrongdoing gingerly, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the usual crossword signal for 'for example'; 'to admit' puts the transgression inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing a car into a space means edging it slowly and carefully.

clue.text: Wicked home in America without love

parts.note: a villa is a house or home

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the other pieces wrap around

parts.note: taken as written
US is short for United States, America
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A loveless American home is a wicked place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, wrapping round the love-zero rather than meaning lacking it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: wicked behaviour is that of a criminal or rogue.

clue.text: Undemonstrative Conservative getting on with it

parts.note: C is short for Conservative in British politics
getting on means growing old

explanation.surface: A reserved Tory politician gets on with the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on' means ageing, not progressing; 'with it' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undemonstrative is reserved and distant, without warmth or affection.

clue.text: Blighters start to court publicity

indicators.note: start to asks for the opening letter of the word court

parts.note: ads are advertisements, publicity

explanation.surface: Rotters begin to seek attention in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' gives C from 'court'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated British insults for dishonourable or contemptible men.

clue.text: Artist holding recipe for soup

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other

parts.note: Hieronymus Bosch was a Dutch painter
R is an abbreviation for recipe, as on a prescription

explanation.surface: A painter keeps a recipe for soup.
explanation.walkthrough: R (recipe, from Latin, as on old prescriptions) goes inside BOSCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetroot soup from Eastern Europe, often served with sour cream.

clue.text: Bell sounds for fight

definitions.meaning: the chiming noise a bell makes

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase imitates the chime of bells, and in British slang means a heated quarrel or punch-up.
